v8.title: Claude Code Insights (local /insights history)
v8.description: Claude Code's own /insights command, computed rather than narrated. Reads claude_insights_sessions, which claude_insights_export.py fills from the local ~/.claude/usage-data/{session-meta,facets} caches /insights already wrote on this machine -- per developer, per machine, the same limitation chronicle has on the Copilot side. See claude_insights_export.py and README.md's Chronicle section for the full story.

panels.title: Sessions /insights has analysed
panels.description: One row per session_id in `claude_insights_sessions`, which `claude_insights_export.py` fills from Claude Code's own local `/insights` cache -- nothing here is inferred, it is what `/insights` already computed the last time it ran on this machine. Deduplicated by keeping only the newest row per `session_id` (highest `captured_at`), because a re-run of `claude_insights_export.py` after `/insights` re-analyses a session sends a full replacement row rather than a delta, and OpenObserve has no upsert -- see the export script's module docstring.

queries.query:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT session_id, MAX(captured_at) AS cap
  FROM claude_insights_sessions
  WHERE service_user IN (${developer}) AND service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  GROUP BY session_id
),
sessions AS (
  SELECT s.* FROM claude_insights_sessions s
  JOIN latest l ON l.session_id = s.session_id AND l.cap = s.captured_at
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) AS "y_axis_1" FROM sessions

panels.title: Average session length (minutes)
panels.description: `duration_minutes` from session-meta -- the span between a session's first and last event, mechanical and free, the same figure `/insights` itself reports as part of its own summary. Deduplicated by keeping only the newest row per `session_id` (highest `captured_at`), because a re-run of `claude_insights_export.py` after `/insights` re-analyses a session sends a full replacement row rather than a delta, and OpenObserve has no upsert -- see the export script's module docstring.

queries.query:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT session_id, MAX(captured_at) AS cap
  FROM claude_insights_sessions
  WHERE service_user IN (${developer}) AND service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  GROUP BY session_id
),
sessions AS (
  SELECT s.* FROM claude_insights_sessions s
  JOIN latest l ON l.session_id = s.session_id AND l.cap = s.captured_at
)
SELECT ROUND(COALESCE(AVG(duration_minutes), 0), 1) AS "y_axis_1" FROM sessions

panels.title: Dissatisfaction rate, of judged sessions (%)
panels.description: Share of the sessions `/insights` sent to the model for judgement (not every session gets one -- see the export script) where `satisfaction_negative` outweighed `satisfaction_positive`. The split comes from `user_satisfaction_counts`, whose keys `claude_insights_export.derive_row` sorts by substring match on dissatisfied/frustrated/unsatisfied -- read that function before trusting a value that looks wrong. Deduplicated by keeping only the newest row per `session_id` (highest `captured_at`), because a re-run of `claude_insights_export.py` after `/insights` re-analyses a session sends a full replacement row rather than a delta, and OpenObserve has no upsert -- see the export script's module docstring.

queries.query:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT session_id, MAX(captured_at) AS cap
  FROM claude_insights_sessions
  WHERE service_user IN (${developer}) AND service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  GROUP BY session_id
),
sessions AS (
  SELECT s.* FROM claude_insights_sessions s
  JOIN latest l ON l.session_id = s.session_id AND l.cap = s.captured_at
)
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN satisfaction_negative > satisfaction_positive THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
             / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN satisfaction_positive IS NOT NULL OR satisfaction_negative IS NOT NULL
                               THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0), 1) AS "y_axis_1"
FROM sessions

panels.title: Sessions that edited files but never committed (%)
panels.description: `files_modified > 0` and `git_commits` is 0 or absent, out of every session that touched a file at all. Work sitting uncommitted at the end of a session is not visible to `git log` and is one session away from being lost. Deduplicated by keeping only the newest row per `session_id` (highest `captured_at`), because a re-run of `claude_insights_export.py` after `/insights` re-analyses a session sends a full replacement row rather than a delta, and OpenObserve has no upsert -- see the export script's module docstring.

queries.query:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT session_id, MAX(captured_at) AS cap
  FROM claude_insights_sessions
  WHERE service_user IN (${developer}) AND service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  GROUP BY session_id
),
sessions AS (
  SELECT s.* FROM claude_insights_sessions s
  JOIN latest l ON l.session_id = s.session_id AND l.cap = s.captured_at
)
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(files_modified, 0) > 0 AND COALESCE(git_commits, 0) = 0
                          THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
             / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(files_modified, 0) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0), 1) AS "y_axis_1"
FROM sessions

panels.title: What to change, ranked
panels.description: Every finding is a threshold over the columns `/insights` already computed -- no model call of this script's own, nothing scheduled beyond running `/insights` and `claude_insights_export.py` yourselves, and the SQL is readable in the panel editor. A rule that is not over threshold returns no row, so an empty panel means there is nothing to act on. Severity is judgement, not measured risk: `high` is worth a look this week, `review` is worth knowing about. Grouped by developer, so it reads the same for one person as for many. Deduplicated by keeping only the newest row per `session_id` (highest `captured_at`), because a re-run of `claude_insights_export.py` after `/insights` re-analyses a session sends a full replacement row rather than a delta, and OpenObserve has no upsert -- see the export script's module docstring.

queries.query:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT session_id, MAX(captured_at) AS cap
  FROM claude_insights_sessions
  WHERE service_user IN (${developer}) AND service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  GROUP BY session_id
),
sessions AS (
  SELECT s.* FROM claude_insights_sessions s
  JOIN latest l ON l.session_id = s.session_id AND l.cap = s.captured_at
),
per_dev AS (
  SELECT service_user AS developer,
         COUNT(*) AS n,
         SUM(CASE WHEN satisfaction_negative > satisfaction_positive THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dissatisfied,
         SUM(CASE WHEN satisfaction_positive IS NOT NULL OR satisfaction_negative IS NOT NULL
                  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS judged,
         SUM(COALESCE(tool_errors, 0)) AS tool_errors,
         SUM(COALESCE(user_message_count, 0)) AS messages,
         SUM(COALESCE(user_interruptions, 0)) AS interruptions,
         SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(files_modified, 0) > 0 AND COALESCE(git_commits, 0) = 0
                  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS uncommitted,
         SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(files_modified, 0) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS edited,
         SUM(COALESCE(uses_task_agent, 0)) AS agent_sessions,
         SUM(COALESCE(uses_mcp, 0)) AS mcp_sessions
  FROM sessions GROUP BY 1),
friction AS (
  SELECT service_user AS developer, primary_friction, COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM sessions WHERE primary_friction IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2),
top_friction_count AS (SELECT developer, MAX(n) AS n FROM friction GROUP BY 1),
top_friction AS (
  -- Max-then-rejoin, not ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ...): a partitioned window is rejected
  -- here with "Expects PARTITION BY expression to be ordered".
  SELECT f.developer AS developer, MAX(f.primary_friction) AS friction, t.n AS n
  FROM friction f JOIN top_friction_count t ON t.developer = f.developer AND t.n = f.n
  GROUP BY f.developer, t.n)
SELECT p.developer AS "developer", '1 high' AS "severity", 'Sessions ending dissatisfied' AS "signal",
       p.dissatisfied || ' of ' || p.judged || ' judged sessions (' ||
       ROUND(100.0 * p.dissatisfied / NULLIF(p.judged, 0), 0) || '%)' AS "measured",
       'Read the friction detail on the dissatisfied sessions below before the pattern repeats.' AS "what_to_do"
FROM per_dev p
WHERE p.judged >= 5 AND 100.0 * p.dissatisfied / NULLIF(p.judged, 0) > 20
UNION ALL
SELECT p.developer, '1 high', 'Tool calls keep failing',
       p.tool_errors || ' tool errors across ' || p.n || ' sessions (' ||
       ROUND(1.0 * p.tool_errors / NULLIF(p.n, 0), 1) || ' per session)',
       'A tool that fails this often is worth checking directly rather than having the agent retry it every session.'
FROM per_dev p
WHERE p.n >= 5 AND 1.0 * p.tool_errors / NULLIF(p.n, 0) > 1
UNION ALL
SELECT p.developer, '2 medium', 'Frequent interruptions',
       p.interruptions || ' interruptions across ' || p.messages || ' prompts (' ||
       ROUND(100.0 * p.interruptions / NULLIF(p.messages, 0), 0) || '%)',
       'Stopping the agent mid-task usually means the ask was underspecified. A short plan up front costs less than the interruption.'
FROM per_dev p
WHERE p.messages >= 20 AND 100.0 * p.interruptions / NULLIF(p.messages, 0) > 10
UNION ALL
SELECT p.developer, '2 medium', 'Edits made without a commit',
       p.uncommitted || ' of ' || p.edited || ' sessions that touched files (' ||
       ROUND(100.0 * p.uncommitted / NULLIF(p.edited, 0), 0) || '%)',
       'Work sitting uncommitted at the end of a session is not visible to git log and is one session away from being lost.'
FROM per_dev p
WHERE p.edited >= 5 AND 100.0 * p.uncommitted / NULLIF(p.edited, 0) > 50
UNION ALL
SELECT p.developer, '3 review', 'One friction pattern keeps recurring',
       t.n || ' of ' || p.judged || ' judged sessions logged "' || t.friction || '"',
       'The same friction repeating is usually worth fixing once rather than working around every time.'
FROM per_dev p JOIN top_friction t ON t.developer = p.developer
WHERE p.judged >= 5 AND 100.0 * t.n / NULLIF(p.judged, 0) > 25
UNION ALL
SELECT p.developer, '3 review', 'Sub-agents and MCP tools barely used',
       p.agent_sessions || ' of ' || p.n || ' sessions used a sub-agent, ' || p.mcp_sessions || ' used MCP',
       'Not wrong, but delegation and MCP tools are often the cheaper way to do the same task -- worth trying once.'
FROM per_dev p
WHERE p.n >= 10 AND p.agent_sessions = 0 AND p.mcp_sessions = 0
ORDER BY "severity", "developer"

panels.title: Sessions over time, by outcome
panels.description: One bar per day sessions started (`_timestamp` is the session's own `start_time`, not when this script ran), split by `outcome` -- the model's own verdict on whether the session's goal was reached. Sessions `/insights` never sent for judgement show as 'not yet judged' rather than being dropped. Deduplicated by keeping only the newest row per `session_id` (highest `captured_at`), because a re-run of `claude_insights_export.py` after `/insights` re-analyses a session sends a full replacement row rather than a delta, and OpenObserve has no upsert -- see the export script's module docstring.

queries.query:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT session_id, MAX(captured_at) AS cap
  FROM claude_insights_sessions
  WHERE service_user IN (${developer}) AND service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  GROUP BY session_id
),
sessions AS (
  SELECT s.* FROM claude_insights_sessions s
  JOIN latest l ON l.session_id = s.session_id AND l.cap = s.captured_at
)
SELECT date_trunc('day', to_timestamp_micros(_timestamp)) AS "x_axis_1",
       COUNT(*) AS "y_axis_1",
       COALESCE(outcome, 'not yet judged') AS "breakdown_1"
FROM sessions
GROUP BY x_axis_1, breakdown_1
ORDER BY x_axis_1

panels.title: Every developer
panels.description: Sessions, average length, dissatisfaction rate and tool errors per developer, plus whether they have tried delegation (sub-agents) or MCP tools at all. The table a lead reads first. Deduplicated by keeping only the newest row per `session_id` (highest `captured_at`), because a re-run of `claude_insights_export.py` after `/insights` re-analyses a session sends a full replacement row rather than a delta, and OpenObserve has no upsert -- see the export script's module docstring.

queries.query:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT session_id, MAX(captured_at) AS cap
  FROM claude_insights_sessions
  WHERE service_user IN (${developer}) AND service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  GROUP BY session_id
),
sessions AS (
  SELECT s.* FROM claude_insights_sessions s
  JOIN latest l ON l.session_id = s.session_id AND l.cap = s.captured_at
)
SELECT service_user AS developer,
       COUNT(*) AS sessions,
       ROUND(AVG(duration_minutes), 1) AS avg_minutes,
       SUM(CASE WHEN satisfaction_positive IS NOT NULL OR satisfaction_negative IS NOT NULL
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS judged_sessions,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN satisfaction_negative > satisfaction_positive THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
             / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN satisfaction_positive IS NOT NULL OR satisfaction_negative IS NOT NULL
                              THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0), 1) AS dissatisfaction_percent,
       SUM(COALESCE(tool_errors, 0)) AS tool_errors,
       SUM(COALESCE(git_commits, 0)) AS git_commits,
       SUM(COALESCE(uses_task_agent, 0)) AS sessions_using_a_subagent,
       SUM(COALESCE(uses_mcp, 0)) AS sessions_using_mcp
FROM sessions
GROUP BY developer
ORDER BY sessions DESC

panels.title: What sessions were for
panels.description: One row per `primary_goal_category` -- the most-represented key in the model's own `goal_categories` map for that session, picked by `claude_insights_export.derive_row`. Only covers judged sessions; a session `/insights` never analysed has no goal category and is not in this table. Deduplicated by keeping only the newest row per `session_id` (highest `captured_at`), because a re-run of `claude_insights_export.py` after `/insights` re-analyses a session sends a full replacement row rather than a delta, and OpenObserve has no upsert -- see the export script's module docstring.

queries.query:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT session_id, MAX(captured_at) AS cap
  FROM claude_insights_sessions
  WHERE service_user IN (${developer}) AND service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  GROUP BY session_id
),
sessions AS (
  SELECT s.* FROM claude_insights_sessions s
  JOIN latest l ON l.session_id = s.session_id AND l.cap = s.captured_at
)
SELECT primary_goal_category AS goal_category,
       COUNT(*) AS sessions,
       ROUND(AVG(duration_minutes), 1) AS avg_minutes,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN satisfaction_negative > satisfaction_positive THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
             / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1) AS dissatisfaction_percent
FROM sessions
WHERE primary_goal_category IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY goal_category
ORDER BY sessions DESC

panels.title: Friction, by kind
panels.description: One row per `primary_friction` the model logged, with one example detail per kind -- picked by `MAX(friction_detail)`, so it is one real example rather than the most common wording, not a summary of the group. Empty if no judged session in range hit friction at all, which is a reading worth taking at face value. Deduplicated by keeping only the newest row per `session_id` (highest `captured_at`), because a re-run of `claude_insights_export.py` after `/insights` re-analyses a session sends a full replacement row rather than a delta, and OpenObserve has no upsert -- see the export script's module docstring.

queries.query:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT session_id, MAX(captured_at) AS cap
  FROM claude_insights_sessions
  WHERE service_user IN (${developer}) AND service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  GROUP BY session_id
),
sessions AS (
  SELECT s.* FROM claude_insights_sessions s
  JOIN latest l ON l.session_id = s.session_id AND l.cap = s.captured_at
)
SELECT primary_friction AS friction,
       COUNT(*) AS sessions,
       MAX(friction_detail) AS example
FROM sessions
WHERE primary_friction IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY friction
ORDER BY sessions DESC

panels.title: Latest sessions, most recent first
panels.description: One row per session, newest `start_time` first: what it was for, how it went, and the model's own one-line summary where a judgement exists. `brief_summary` is prose the model wrote about someone's work -- read a row before putting this panel where people other than that developer can see it, the same caution the chronicle dashboard's advice panels carry. Deduplicated by keeping only the newest row per `session_id` (highest `captured_at`), because a re-run of `claude_insights_export.py` after `/insights` re-analyses a session sends a full replacement row rather than a delta, and OpenObserve has no upsert -- see the export script's module docstring.

queries.query:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT session_id, MAX(captured_at) AS cap
  FROM claude_insights_sessions
  WHERE service_user IN (${developer}) AND service_user <> 'schema_seed'
  GROUP BY session_id
),
sessions AS (
  SELECT s.* FROM claude_insights_sessions s
  JOIN latest l ON l.session_id = s.session_id AND l.cap = s.captured_at
)
SELECT service_user AS developer,
       to_char(to_timestamp_micros(_timestamp), '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M') AS started,
       project_path,
       duration_minutes,
       COALESCE(outcome, 'not judged') AS outcome,
       COALESCE(claude_helpfulness, '') AS helpfulness,
       COALESCE(brief_summary, first_prompt, '') AS summary
FROM sessions
ORDER BY _timestamp DESC
LIMIT 60
